children: Mortgage rates fell for the third consecutive week, but demand remained subdued as prospective borrowers hold off on decisions until rates, economic, and political conditions settle.
30-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.18% as of November 5, down from 7.24% last week and above the year-ago level of 6.22%,
the Freddie Mac Weekly Mortgage Applications Survey.
15-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 6.57%, down 6.60% a week ago and above 5.50% a year ago.

"Mortgage rates continued their downward trajectory this week, improving the environment for prospective homebuyers against a backdrop of strong economic growth," said Freddie Mac's chief economist, Sam Khater.

"Mortgage application activity remained subdued last week despite rates falling to their lowest level since September. Purchase applications decreased and refinance activity remained largely unchanged, with both much lower than year-ago levels. Prospective borrowers may be holding off decisions until rates and economic and political conditions settle," said Mortgage Bankers Association's CEO Bob Broeksmit.

title: Mortgage rates down for third straight week
